_about.what: What each nation's bombers carry to tell one from another (bomber-marks.ts; the historian's note of 20 November 2026, historian/bomber-tours-identity.md). Only American bombers carry a name and nose art (Brian, 20 November 2026: 'nose art only for US bombers, other countries didnt do that'). Every other nation's carry the marking their air force painted, and every nation's carry a tally: a bomb for each mission and a mark for each aircraft shot down.
_about.letter: Britain and the Commonwealth: two squadron letters and the aircraft's own letter ('KM-G'), called by the letter's word ('G for George'). 'early' are the words to the end of 1942 and 'late' those from 'from' on. 'block' are squadron letters never given: PO and AR are kept clear of two famous Lancasters, the rest read badly. 'never' are a famous real aircraft's letters, a squadron's two ('AJ', the dams raid) or one aircraft's whole marking ('KM-B'): a bomber whose turn it would be wears the last letters in its group's order instead.
_about.code: Germany: the wing's two characters, then the aircraft's letter and its squadron's letter ('5J+DM'). 'aircraft' are the aircraft letters of one squadron, 'squadrons' the squadron letters of one wing, 'words' the radio word for each letter of the alphabet.
_about.tail: Japan: a unit code and the aircraft's number on the tail ('K-312'). 'codes' are the unit codes, 'first' the first number and 'per' how many aircraft carry one code. 'never' are two famous real aircraft's markings: a bomber whose turn it would be carries a number 'per' higher instead.
_about.squadron: Italy: the squadron's number and the aircraft's ('278-7'). A group's squadrons are numbered on from a number between 'from' and 'to', 'per' aircraft each.
_about.tactical: The Soviet Union: a number painted in one of 'colours', 'per' aircraft to a colour ('White 23').
